Vitest Browser API listening on all interfaces (CVE-2026-53633 pre-condition) AIWeaponization High
Hunts for Vitest Browser Mode launched with browser.api.host=0.0.0.0, which exposes the CDP-capable WebSocket RPC to the network. Per CVE-2026-53633, this is the deploy-time misconfiguration that turns the local-only CDP bridge into a remotely exploitable RCE pre-condition, even when allowWrite/allowExec are false. Rationale: Pivots on the exact flag combo named in the article repro (`api: { host: '0.0.0.0' }`) plus the vitest/@vitest/browser/vite-plus package names from the GHSA affected-packages list. Article explicitly identifies this as the network-exposure precondition.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit developer intentionally exposing Vitest to a teammate over LAN for pair-debugging
  • CI runners that bind Vitest to 0.0.0.0 inside a container by design
  • Docker-compose dev stacks where 0.0.0.0 is required for port-forwarding to host
  • E2E test rigs that deliberately expose the browser API to a remote orchestrator
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("build-","ci-","runner-") and AccountName has_any ("ci","build","jenkins","github-actions"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the host is a developer/CI workstation and identify whether the bind to 0.0.0.0 was intentional. Check ProcessCommandLine for whether allowWrite/allowExec are also present and what their values are. Capture the parent process and the package.json scripts that launched node. Step 2 (contain): If unintentional, kill the node.exe PID and block inbound 63315 (or the discovered Vitest port) at the host firewall. If intentional, scope exposure: is the dev machine reachable from VPN/internet? Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceNetworkEvents for any non-loopback inbound connections to that PID's listening port during its lifetime, and pivot on DeviceFileEvents for writes to vite.config.* or vitest.config.* by browser processes on the same host within the same session.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "browser.api.host" and ProcessCommandLine has "0.0.0.0"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where CommandLine has "browser.api.host" and CommandLine has "0.0.0.0"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Vitest Browser API Listening on All Interfaces (CVE-2026-53633)
id: 7c1a9f4e-2b3a-4d2c-9e0e-9b1d8c4f1e23
description: Detects node.exe launched as Vitest Browser Mode with browser.api.host=0.0.0.0, exposing the CDP-capable WebSocket RPC to the network and creating the pre-condition for CVE-2026-53633 RCE.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\node.exe'
  selection_cmd_vitest:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'vitest'
      - '@vitest/browser'
      - 'vite-plus'
  selection_cmd_host:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'browser.api.host'
      - '0.0.0.0'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd_vitest and selection_cmd_host
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) (@CommandLine:*vitest* OR @CommandLine:*"@vitest/browser"* OR @CommandLine:*vite-plus*) @CommandLine:*browser.api.host* @CommandLine:*0.0.0.0*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(vitest|@vitest\/browser|vite-plus)/i
| CommandLine=/browser\.api\.host/i
| CommandLine=/0\.0\.0\.0/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" Processes.process="*vitest*" Processes.process="*browser.api.host*" Processes.process="*0.0.0.0*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" Processes.process="*vitest*" Processes.process="*browser.api.host*" Processes.process="*0.0.0.0*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Inbound non-loopback connection to Vitest browser API listener (TCP/63315) AIDelivery High
Detects external/non-loopback inbound connections accepted by node.exe on TCP/63315, the default Vitest browser API port per the article. Reaching the listener is a prerequisite for the CDP-via-WebSocket exploit chain in CVE-2026-53633. Rationale: 63315 is the literal port shown in the article's repro (`http://localhost:63315`). Combining listener-side process identity (node.exe running vitest) with non-loopback remote source is the article-specific signal — generic 'port 63315 open' alone would be noisier.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer pair-programming where a teammate hits the colleague's dev server over LAN
  • Container-to-container traffic inside a docker-compose dev environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys) probing the high port
  • E2E test orchestrators in CI connecting to the spawned Vitest browser API
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteIP startswith "10." or RemoteIP startswith "192.168." or RemoteIP startswith "172.16." or RemoteIP startswith "172.17." or RemoteIP startswith "172.18.")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the remote IP, geolocate, and check whether it's a known dev/CI peer or external. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the receiving node.exe to confirm Vitest Browser Mode and whether host=0.0.0.0 was set. Step 2 (contain): Block 63315 inbound at the host firewall, kill the node.exe listener, and rotate any source-controlled secrets that the project root may contain. Step 3 (hunt): Within the connection window, look for DeviceFileEvents writing `vite.config.*` / `vitest.config.*` files initiated by a browser binary (chrome/chromium/msedge/headless_shell), and pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any node.exe child shell/LOLBin spawned in the next 60 seconds — those are the post-exploitation signals.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ListeningConnectionCreated","ConnectionAccepted")
| where LocalPort == 63315
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !startswith "169.254"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemoteIPType, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 63315
| where NetworkDirection =~ "Inbound"
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr) and SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1" and not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcPortNumber, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @DestinationPort:63315 NOT CIDR(@SourceIp, 127.0.0.0/8) NOT CIDR(@SourceIp, ::1/128)

Vitest false-sense-of-security config: allowWrite/allowExec false but CDP bridge exposed AIWeaponization High
Detects the precise dangerous configuration the CVE-2026-53633 advisory calls out: Vitest started with allowWrite:false and allowExec:false (operator believes it is safe) while host is bound externally, exposing the CDP RPC that bypasses both flags. Higher-fidelity than the bare 0.0.0.0 hunt because it captures intent + the gap. Rationale: Targets the literal misconfiguration the advisory names: 'In a verified reproduction with allowWrite: false and allowExec: false, CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior set the browser download directory...'. Three-flag combo (host=0.0.0.0 + allowWrite=false + allowExec=false) is rarer than any single flag and reads as 'thought-they-were-safe operator'.
ATT&CKT1190 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit dev who copy-pasted the GHSA reproduction config verbatim to verify their own exposure
  • Security researcher running a local PoC for the CVE
  • Teams who set the flags as a hardening attempt without realising the CDP gap
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the user is a developer and ask whether they intentionally exposed the API while disabling write/exec — explain the CDP bypass and link the GHSA. Step 2 (contain): Have them either upgrade @vitest/browser past the patched version (>5.0.0-beta.3, fix on the 4.x/3.x lines per advisory) OR bind to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0. Step 3 (hunt): On the same host within the listener's lifetime, search DeviceNetworkEvents for non-loopback inbound to the discovered port and DeviceFileEvents for `vite.config.*` writes by a browser binary — those would indicate the misconfiguration was actually weaponised.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowWrite\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowExec\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "browser.api.host" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("0.0.0.0","::")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowCDP\s*[:=]\s*false")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowWrite\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowExec\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where CommandLine has "browser.api.host" and (CommandLine has "0.0.0.0" or CommandLine has "::")
| where not(CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowCDP\s*[:=]\s*false")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

vite/vitest config file modified by browser-context process (CVE-2026-53633 payload drop) AIInstallation High
Detects creation or modification of vite.config.* or vitest.config.* files where the writing process is a browser binary (chromium/chrome/msedge/headless_shell/firefox/playwright). This is the verified impact described in the advisory — CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior + Runtime.evaluate causes the browser to 'download' a malicious vite.config.ts into the project root, which Vitest then reloads and executes. Rationale: Uses the exact file targeted in the advisory repro (`vite.config.ts`, written via `<a download="vite.config.ts">`) plus the CDP-capable browser binaries the advisory names (Playwright Chromium). A browser writing a build-system config file in a project root is anomalous regardless of CVE — and for this specific vector it's the smoking gun.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using a browser-based 'Save As' to manually overwrite their own config (rare and observable)
  • Web IDE / StackBlitz-style PWAs writing project files via the File System Access API
  • Browser extensions like 'Save All Resources' grabbing dev assets that happen to be named vite.config.ts
  • Visual config-editor UIs that emit a downloaded config (treat as policy violation)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Diff the new vite.config.* against version control (git log/blame on the file). Any non-developer-authored changes — process.spawn, child_process, http imports, eval, dynamic require — confirm the exploit. Capture file SHA256, FileOriginUrl, and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine to recover the spawning Playwright/Chromium invocation. Step 2 (contain): Kill the Vitest node.exe parent immediately (config-reload hasn't necessarily fired yet); revert the config from git; block 63315 inbound at the host firewall; rotate any secrets the project root exposed (npm tokens, .env files, AWS creds, SSH keys). Step 3 (hunt): Within the next 60 seconds of the file write, look for node.exe spawning shells / LOLBins (cmd, powershell, sh, bash, curl, wget, certutil) and for outbound network from node.exe to non-corp destinations — those indicate the config-reload-to-RCE step fired.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, PreviousFileName, PreviousFolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileOriginUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WebSocket access to Vitest browser API tester endpoint (CVE-2026-53633 exploit signature) AIExploitation High
Hunts proxy/WAF/IDS records for HTTP-upgrade or HTTP requests targeting `/__vitest_browser_api__?type=tester` or the `/__vitest_test__/` runner page on port 63315. The advisory's step 3 shows the literal URI used to authenticate to the CDP RPC bridge as a tester client, which is the active-exploit signature. Rationale: Pivots on the literal URI path `/__vitest_browser_api__?type=tester` and the runner page `/__vitest_test__/` quoted verbatim in the advisory's repro steps 1 and 3, plus the `sendCdpEvent` RPC method name from step 4. These strings will not appear in legitimate traffic.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vitest's own browser session connecting to its own API (loopback only — filter)
  • Internal CI runners visiting the Vitest UI for debugging via the official `?type=client` (not `tester`) flow
  • Documentation pages on the Vitest site referencing the path strings (in user-agent of a researcher's browser)
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !startswith "127." and SourceIP != "::1"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify SourceIP — was the access from loopback (legit Vitest internal) or a remote IP? Pull the full URL chain to extract sessionId, projectName, projectName and confirm the format matches the advisory's tester URL shape. Step 2 (contain): If remote, block source IP at perimeter, force-kill the receiving Vitest node.exe, and treat the workstation as compromised pending DFIR. Rotate any project-root secrets and the npm/pnpm tokens cached on the host. Step 3 (hunt): Within the same connection window, hunt for `vite.config.*` writes by a browser process on the destination host (UC4), node.exe spawning child shells (UC6), and additional CDP method names in payloads (`Page.setDownloadBehavior`, `Runtime.evaluate`) via deep packet inspection or Zeek `ws.message` records.
DeviceNetworkEvents

| order by Timestamp desc

Config-reload RCE: node.exe spawns shell/LOLBin within 30s of vite/vitest config write AIExploitation High
Temporal correlation that catches the CVE-2026-53633 RCE moment: vite.config.* is overwritten, Vitest's HMR reloads the new config, and the Node.js payload spawns cmd/powershell/bash/curl/etc. The short window (≤30s) plus the node parent disambiguates legitimate dev-script execution from exploit-triggered execution. Rationale: Models the article's verified RCE chain explicitly: 'vite.config.ts is overwritten with attacker-controlled content. Vitest reloads the changed config. The injected Node.js payload runs on the host.' Constrains parent node.exe to a Vitest invocation (rules out generic npm-script shell spawns) and bounds the delta to 30s (the HMR reload window) to keep precision high.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually editing vite.config in an editor and triggering an npm script that legitimately spawns a shell as part of hot-reload
  • Vitest's own postinstall / test-setup scripts that shell out (e.g. running a docker-compose up via execa)
  • HMR config reload triggering a legitimate `child_process.spawn` in a project that intentionally calls out (rare; review per project)
  • Webpack/Vite plugins that spawn helper processes (graphql codegen, prisma generate) on config change
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has_any ("prisma generate","graphql-codegen","docker-compose","esbuild","tsc --build","husky install") and ConfigWriter !in~ ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the ChildCmd and NodeCmd from the alert. If ChildCmd is a known build helper (codegen, docker, prisma) chained off an explicit script in package.json, demote. If ChildCmd is a download (curl/wget/certutil/bitsadmin) or contains base64/encoded payloads, treat as confirmed RCE. Diff the new vite.config.* against git to recover the injected payload. Step 2 (contain): Kill the node.exe process tree, isolate the host (network containment / EDR isolate), and revert the config from git. Rotate every credential the developer's session could have touched: SSH keys, AWS keys, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, browser-stored cookies. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot DeviceNetworkEvents off the child PID for C2 callbacks; search the entire dev-team device fleet for any vite.config.* write by a browser binary (UC4) and any inbound to 63315 (UC2) in the past 30 days; check the same dev's commit history for accidental commit of the poisoned config.
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let ConfigWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
    | project ConfigWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ConfigPath = FolderPath, ConfigFile = FileName, ConfigWriter = InitiatingProcessFileName, WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite")
    | where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","netsh.exe")
    | project ChildSpawnTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, NodeFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
) on DeviceId
| where ChildSpawnTime between (ConfigWriteTime .. ConfigWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ChildSpawnTime, ConfigWriteTime)
| project ConfigWriteTime, ChildSpawnTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, ConfigPath, ConfigFile, ConfigWriter, WriterCmd, ChildProcess, ChildCmd, NodeCmd
| order by ConfigWriteTime desc
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let ConfigWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
    | project ConfigWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ConfigPath = TargetFilePath, ConfigFile = TargetFileName, ConfigWriter = ActingProcessName;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has "node.exe"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
    | project ChildSpawnTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ChildProcess = ActingProcessName, ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, NodeCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
) on DvcHostname
| where ChildSpawnTime between (ConfigWriteTime .. ConfigWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ChildSpawnTime, ConfigWriteTime)
| project ConfigWriteTime, ChildSpawnTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath, ConfigFile, ConfigWriter, ChildProcess, ChildCmd, NodeCmd
| order by ConfigWriteTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:*vitest* @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\wmic.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/node\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|bash|sh|wmic|curl|wget|bitsadmin|certutil|rundll32|regsvr32)\.exe$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/(vitest|@vitest\/browser|vite-plus)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$/i}, field=aid, include=[ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("node.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
Critical

Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails

The Hacker News
2026-06-15 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email. The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process

UNC6508 Google Workspace Domain Content Compliance Rule with External BCC AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation/modification of Google Workspace domain-level content compliance rules that silently BCC matching messages to an external (Gmail) address. UNC6508 used exactly this admin feature for stealth exfiltration without dropping malware on the mail tier. Rationale: GTIG report explicitly names domain content compliance rules with BCC to a Gmail address as UNC6508's exfiltration vector. The detection keys on admin operation + content_compliance subject + BCC/forward verb + external-domain destination — every component is article-supplied. Cross-checked against MITRE T1098.002 / T1114.003 and existing Sigma rules (no overlap for the GSuite content_compliance + BCC combo). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/ • https://services.google.com/fh/files/blogs/google-threat-intel-defense-sector-report.pdf
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1114.003 T1556
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate compliance program BCCing to a corporate journaling mailbox (often on a different domain)
  • DLP rule that quarantines outbound mail to a legal-hold archive address
  • Migration tooling creating temporary forward-to-Gmail rules during a tenant cutover
  • Approved e-discovery vendor adding a journal rule to its own collection mailbox
  • MSP/MSSP onboarding scripts standing up compliance copies for monitoring
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has_any ("compliance@","legal@","ediscovery@","journal@") and RawText has_any ("proofpoint.com","mimecast.com","barracuda.com","global-relay.com"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the rule via Admin SDK and verify the destination address, keyword list, and creating admin. Compare the source IP/UserAgent of the admin action against that admin's normal sign-in pattern in SigninLogs/AADSignInEventsBeta. Step 2 (contain): Disable the rule (do not delete — preserve for forensics), revoke active sessions for the creating admin account, force password reset + step-up MFA, and check for any sibling rules created in the same window. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the creating admin's recent activity for new OAuth grants, app passwords, super-admin role assignments; review the keyword list against your sensitive-data taxonomy; pull all mail audit log entries showing BCC delivery to the destination address since rule creation and notify legal/IR.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where IsAdminOperation == true
| where ActionType has_any ("CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING","Create rule","Update rule","compliance","CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING","CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| where RawText has_any ("content_compliance","CONTENT_COMPLIANCE","content compliance","contentCompliance")
| where RawText has_any ("BCC","Bcc","bcc","forward","copyMessage")
| where RawText has "gmail.com" or RawText matches regex @"@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, RawText
let ExternalDomainPattern = @"@(?!yourorg\.com$)[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}";
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING","CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING","create_rule","content_compliance")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| where Raw has_any ("content_compliance","contentCompliance","CONTENT_COMPLIANCE")
| where Raw has_any ("BCC","Bcc","bcc","forward","copyMessage")
| where Raw matches regex ExternalDomainPattern
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, Raw

UNC6508 Content Compliance Rule with Espionage Keywords (Patroit / chikungunya) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation of GWS content compliance / forwarding rules whose keyword list overlaps UNC6508's published collection priorities — the misspelled 'Patroit' tag, 'chikungunya' (highly specific to the 2025 Guangdong outbreak the actor watched), uncrewed vehicles, and offensive-cyber terminology. Rationale: Article gives a highly specific keyword the actor used ('Patroit' — note the misspelling) plus 'chikungunya' (linked to the 2025 Guangdong outbreak the actor was watching). These two strings alone are near-zero-FP in legitimate compliance rules. Adds CUI/FOUO/ITAR as defense-research analogues per article's collection-priority list. Cross-checked against: • https://services.google.com/fh/files/blogs/google-threat-intel-defense-sector-report.pdf • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1213
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red team simulating UNC6508 with the same keyword list
  • Threat-intel team setting up canary rules using published IOCs
  • Research librarian creating an alerting rule for a literature watch on chikungunya (medical research orgs only)
  • Compliance team building a CUI/FOUO data-loss rule that legitimately uses those terms
  • DLP policy migration that imports a published keyword pack
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has "redteam" or AccountDisplayName has "purple-team" or RawText has "canary")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full rule definition (keyword list + destination). If 'Patroit' or 'chikungunya' appear, treat as TP until proven otherwise — these are signature of UNC6508. Verify creating admin's last 30 days of activity. Step 2 (contain): Disable the rule but preserve definition, revoke admin sessions, rotate admin credentials, enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all super-admins, and audit Workspace super-admin role assignments since September 2023 (earliest known UNC6508 dwell). Step 3 (hunt): Search 90 days of mail audit logs for BCC delivery to any address in the destination list; pivot on any REDCap-hosting servers in the org for INFINITERED hashes; engage Google Workspace security and GTIG for IOC enrichment.

Outbound Connection to UNC6508 C2 Infrastructure (23.169.65.49) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects any host-side connection to 23.169.65.49 — the UNC6508 C2 IP that INFINITERED uses for HTTP-cookie command tasking. Article-provided IOC; high-confidence on any inbound or outbound hit. Rationale: 23.169.65.49 is the only IP indicator the article provides for UNC6508 / INFINITERED C2. Direct IOC match, no derivation needed. Cross-referenced MITRE for T1071.001 + T1102 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / sandbox sandbox host detonating the IOC for analysis
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion box that resolves indicators to enrich
  • NAT/proxy egress shared with other tenants where the IP is reused by a benign service later
  • Red-team purple exercise replaying the IOC
  • Internet-wide scanner traffic (rare for outbound but possible for inbound)
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab","ti-enrich"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm direction (inbound to a REDCap server vs outbound from a workstation — the article describes both shapes). Pull the initiating process, account, and parent. For inbound, capture the HTTP cookie value if proxy/WAF logs are available. Step 2 (contain): Block 23.169.65.49 at perimeter + EDR network containment for hits; isolate the host pending IR triage. Step 3 (hunt): Hash-match the seven INFINITERED SHA256s on the host's filesystem; pivot REDCap install path for trojanized system files; review domain admin authentication trail for the dwell window (Sept 2023 onward); audit GWS content compliance rules per UC #1.

(ImNetworkSession

  | where DstIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" or SrcIpAddr == "23.169.65.49"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where RemoteIp == "23.169.65.49"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)

INFINITERED Trojanized REDCap System File on Disk (SHA256) AIInstallation Medium
Hash-matches the seven INFINITERED SHA256s GTIG published. Catches trojanized REDCap PHP/system files dropped during the install hijack stage, including persistence across upgrades. Rationale: Direct hash IOC from the article (all seven INFINITERED SHA256s pre-extracted). Hash matches are the highest-fidelity signal possible — single-source FP probability ~zero. Falcon LogScale query targets FileWritten because REDCap servers are typically Linux PHP, where INFINITERED trojanizes system files on disk before execution. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel team uploading the hash to a malware sandbox for analysis
  • Security tool downloading the IOC list locally for offline scanning
  • Lab/sandbox detonation of the published IOCs
  • Incident-response analyst staging samples for reverse engineering
  • Backup system replicating quarantined files between sandbox hosts
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab","ti-research") or FolderPath has_any ("\\quarantine\\","\\samples\\","/quarantine/","/samples/"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify whether the host is a production REDCap server. If so, treat as confirmed compromise — INFINITERED reinjects on upgrade, so 'newest version' is not safe. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, snapshot disk + memory, kill the web service, block any C2 IPs at perimeter, and preserve the trojanized files for IR. Do NOT just reinstall REDCap — article notes the upgrade-hijack persistence. Step 3 (hunt): Search all internet-facing REDCap servers for the same hashes; review server access logs for the dwell window (back to Sept 2023); audit local DB tables for stolen credential dumps stored by INFINITERED; rotate every credential ever used to log into the affected REDCap instances; pivot to GWS audit logs per UCs #1/#2.

union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where SHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where SHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName)

union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)

Gmail User-Level Forwarding/Filter Rule to External Address AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects creation of per-user Gmail forwarding or filter-with-forward rules whose destination is outside the org's primary domain — the user-tier analog of the domain content compliance rule UNC6508 abused, and a common companion persistence mechanism if domain-level rules get detected and removed. Rationale: Article reviewer flagged that GWS 'rules' includes user-level forwarding/filters as a sibling persistence path; article explicitly recommends auditing 'mail-forwarding rules' alongside content compliance. External-domain extraction with org-domain anti-filter is the standard high-fidelity shape. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/ • https://support.google.com/a/answer/9300435
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1098.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately forwarding work mail to a personal/recovery account during PTO
  • Approved partner integration that forwards mail to a vendor inbox
  • Departing employee setting an external out-of-office forward
  • Test/QA account configured to forward to an external test inbox
  • User signing up for a third-party SaaS that requires email forwarding for ticketing
Suppression filter
| where not (FwdDomain in ("gmail.com","outlook.com","yahoo.com") and AccountDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)test|qa|sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm whether the forward destination is on an approved list or the user's own recovery address (admin SDK lookup). Compare creation IP/UserAgent to user baseline. Step 2 (contain): If suspicious, disable the rule, revoke active sessions, force MFA re-enrollment, and notify the user. Step 3 (hunt): Search sibling accounts in the same team/department for new external forwards (UNC6508 created bulk rules); pivot to AAD/Workspace sign-ins for the user across the prior 90 days; check for delegation grants (UC #6) created by the same admin.
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where ActionType has_any ("email_forwarding_out_of_domain","Create Filter","Email forwarding","FORWARDING_RULE","CHANGE_USER_SETTING")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| where RawText has_any ("forward","forwardingAddress","FORWARD")
| extend FwdDomain = tolower(extract(@"forward[^@]{0,40}@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, RawText))
| where isnotempty(FwdDomain)
| where not(FwdDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, FwdDomain, RawText
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_FILTER","email_forwarding_out_of_domain","CHANGE_USER_SETTING","FORWARDING_RULE")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| where Raw has_any ("forward","forwardingAddress","FORWARD")
| extend FwdDomain = tolower(extract(@"forward[^@]{0,40}@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, Raw))
| where isnotempty(FwdDomain) and not(FwdDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, FwdDomain, Raw
title: Gmail User-Level Forwarding Rule to External Domain

description: Detects per-user Gmail forwarding or filter-forward rule creation pointing to an address outside the organization's owned domains.
references:

  forward:

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.action=created OR All_Changes.action=modified) (All_Changes.object_category="filter" OR All_Changes.object_category="forward" OR All_Changes.change_type="USER_SETTINGS") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "forward.{0,40}@(?<forward_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search forward_domain!="yourorg.com" forward_domain!="yourorg.org" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.action=created OR All_Changes.action=modified) (All_Changes.object_category="filter" OR All_Changes.object_category="forward" OR All_Changes.change_type="USER_SETTINGS") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "forward.{0,40}@(?<forward_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search forward_domain!="yourorg.com" forward_domain!="yourorg.org" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Gmail Mailbox Delegation Granted to External Principal AIActions on Objectives High
Detects Gmail delegation grants (Mail Delegate / SendAs / SendOnBehalfOf) where the delegate identity is outside the org's primary domain — a stealthier post-compromise persistence path than forwarding because it leaves no rule visible in the source mailbox. Rationale: Reviewer-supplied path; article emphasizes UNC6508 used 'rules' broadly post-admin-compromise to copy mail. Delegation grants are functionally equivalent to forwarding but invisible in the mailbox owner's settings UI, making them a likely follow-on after detection of the BCC rule. External-domain anti-filter is the strongest single signal. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/002/ • https://support.google.com/mail/answer/138350
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cross-tenant M&A integration where a parent-org admin gets temporary delegation
  • Executive assistant from a contracted EA service granted delegation
  • Approved external counsel given delegation for e-discovery
  • Departing employee handing off to a contractor with an external email
  • Tenant migration tooling that grants temporary delegate access
Suppression filter
| where not (DelegateDomain in ("approved-partner.com","counsel.example"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm whether the delegate address is on an approved external-collaborator allowlist. Check the granting admin/user's recent sign-in history for impossible travel or new IPs. Step 2 (contain): Revoke the delegation, revoke active sessions for grantor + grantee (if grantee is internal-but-compromised), and rotate the grantor's password + MFA. Step 3 (hunt): Search the prior 90 days for additional delegations granted by the same admin or to the same external address; pivot on the external address against your inbound mail-flow logs and any GWS rule activity (UCs #1, #5); review domain-admin role assignment history.
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where ActionType has_any ("CREATE_DELEGATE","ADD_DELEGATE","DELEGATE_EMAIL","Add mail delegate","mail.delegate")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| extend DelegateAddr = tolower(extract(@"([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, RawText))
| extend DelegateDomain = tostring(split(DelegateAddr, "@")[1])
| where isnotempty(DelegateDomain) and not(DelegateDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, DelegateAddr, DelegateDomain, RawText
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_DELEGATE","ADD_DELEGATE","DELEGATE_EMAIL","mail.delegate")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| extend DelegateAddr = tolower(extract(@"([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, Raw))
| extend DelegateDomain = tostring(split(DelegateAddr, "@")[1])
| where isnotempty(DelegateDomain) and not(DelegateDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, DelegateAddr, DelegateDomain, Raw
title: Gmail Mailbox Delegation to External Principal
id: 5b8e2d44-7c91-4f63-a318-9d4f1c6b5a32
description: Detects Google Workspace mail delegation grants whose delegate address is outside the corporate domain set.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/chinese-hackers-abused-google-workspace.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1098.002
logsource:
  product: gsuite
  service: admin
detection:
  selection:
    eventName:
      - 'CREATE_DELEGATE'
      - 'ADD_DELEGATE'
      - 'DELEGATE_EMAIL'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:gsuite @evt.name:(CREATE_DELEGATE OR ADD_DELEGATE OR DELEGATE_EMAIL) -@event.parameters.DELEGATE_EMAIL:*@yourorg.com*
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as object values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.change_type="DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="CREATE_DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="ADD_DELEGATE") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "delegate.{0,40}@(?<delegate_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search delegate_domain!="yourorg.com" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as object values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.change_type="DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="CREATE_DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="ADD_DELEGATE") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "delegate.{0,40}@(?<delegate_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search delegate_domain!="yourorg.com" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Admin/Service Account Mailbox Fan-Out (Mass Mailbox Access in Short Window) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects an admin or service account accessing N or more distinct mailboxes within a 1-hour window — the precondition for the bulk rule-creation step UNC6508 performed after gaining domain-admin in Workspace. Rationale: Reviewer-supplied; article explicitly states UNC6508 reached domain admin and then created the BCC rule — necessarily implying mass-mailbox visibility either directly or via the admin SDK. Fan-out threshold of 10 distinct mailboxes/hour for admin/service accounts is a P99 anomaly versus typical break-glass admin workflows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/002/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1530 T1114.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate e-discovery search across many custodian mailboxes
  • Org-wide migration tooling enumerating mailboxes during a tenant move
  • Compliance officer running a litigation hold search
  • Backup/archive vendor's service account performing a full sweep
  • Help-desk admin troubleshooting a delivery issue across a distribution list
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has_any ("ediscovery","backup","migration","compliance") or UAs has_any ("Veritas","Mimecast","Proofpoint","Spanning"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the admin/service account and the mailbox set. Cross-check against scheduled e-discovery / migration / backup activity owners. Step 2 (contain): If unexpected, revoke active sessions + OAuth tokens for the account, suspend or rotate credentials, and require step-up phishing-resistant MFA before re-enabling. Step 3 (hunt): Within the same 1-hour window, look for content compliance rule changes (UC #1), per-user forwarding rule additions (UC #5), and delegation grants (UC #6); if any are present, treat as confirmed UNC6508-shape compromise and escalate to IR.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where IsAdminOperation == true or AccountType has_any ("admin","service")
| where ActionType has_any ("View Item","Access","Read mailbox","List Messages","GET_MAILBOX","Impersonate")
| summarize DistinctMailboxes = dcount(ObjectId), Mailboxes = make_set(ObjectName, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountId, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where DistinctMailboxes >= 10
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where UserType in~ ("Admin","Application","ServicePrincipal") or Operation has_any ("Impersonate","GET_MAILBOX","List Messages","View Item")
| summarize DistinctMailboxes = dcount(ObjectId), Mailboxes = make_set(ObjectId, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SrcIPs = make_set(ClientIP, 10) by UserId, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DistinctMailboxes >= 10
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:gsuite (@evt.name:(GET_MAILBOX OR "List Messages" OR Impersonate OR "View Item") @user.is_admin:true)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(All_Changes.object) as distinct_mailboxes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as mailboxes values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" All_Changes.user_category="admin" by All_Changes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where distinct_mailboxes >= 10 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(All_Changes.object) as distinct_mailboxes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as mailboxes values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" All_Changes.user_category="admin" by All_Changes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where distinct_mailboxes >= 10 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents

// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

North Korean Hackers Are Turning Developer Tools Into Malware Delivery Channels

According to a report published by Proofpoint, the threat actor has been found orchestrating phishing campaigns using developer role recruitment or code review themes
