Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] VS Code / Cursor auto-executing shell via tasks.json runOn:folderOpen (Contagious Interview / UNK_DeadDrop) · [LLM] Git hook auto-execution post-clone (Contagious Interview .githooks/pre-commit) · [LLM] DPRK npm supply-chain install (redeem-onchain-sdk / nicegui / period-newline Axios follow-up) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Windows VBScript loader spawning CMD to install malicious VSIX (UNK_DeadDrop Windows chain) · [LLM] Malicious VS Code extension marketplace install (ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev jupyter VSIX) · [LLM] Overlord macOS / Linux loader — osascript fake security prompt + curl to staging · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to UNK_DeadDrop infrastructure (23.137.105.75:5173 and named domains) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
VS Code / Cursor auto-executing shell via tasks.json runOn:folderOpen (Contagious Interview / UNK_DeadDrop) AIDelivery High
Hunts the cornerstone TTP of UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview: a target clones an attacker-controlled GitHub repo and opens it in VS Code or Cursor, at which point a hidden task (often named 'eslint-check') auto-fires a shell/cmd/cscript command via the runOn:folderOpen feature. Detects Code.exe / cursor.exe parenting curl/wget/cmd/powershell/cscript with download-and-execute strings. Rationale: Targets the exact runOn:folderOpen TTP called out as 'the crucial aspect connecting the campaign to Pyongyang' and corroborated by Abstract Security and OpenSourceMalware blogs (the 'eslint-check' task name is the most-observed disguise). Parent of Code.exe/Cursor.exe spawning a shell with download-execute strings is a tight, low-FP signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://www.abstract.security/blog/contagious-interview-tracking-the-vs-code-tasks-infection-vector • https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/tasksjacker-blog-post
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually running a build/lint task via VS Code task runner
  • Code Runner / ESLint / Prettier extension executing legitimate tooling
  • DevContainer initialisation invoking shell setup scripts
  • Yeoman / npx scaffolding spawning cscript/wscript on Windows
  • Salt-stack / Ansible playbooks invoked from VS Code terminal
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--extensionDevelopmentPath","--inspect-extensions") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm run lint","npm run build","yarn build","vite build"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine + InitiatingProcessCommandLine and inspect the workspace. Use DeviceFileEvents to find .vscode/tasks.json or .githooks/pre-commit written in the last 24h on the same DeviceId — confirm a 'runOn':'folderOpen' or curl|wget pipeline is present. 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, kill the spawned process tree, and revoke any developer credentials accessible from the workstation (GitHub PAT, AWS keys, npm tokens, browser-stored wallet creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 of the spawned shell to find sibling infections, query EmailUrlInfo for github.com/<actor> links in the past 30 days, and search DeviceNetworkEvents for the article's C2 (23.137.105.75:5173) and domain set across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint-check","runOn","folderOpen","| sh","| bash","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","curl -s","wget -q")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint-check","folderOpen","| sh","| bash","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code or Cursor Auto-Executing Shell via tasks.json runOn folderOpen
id: 8c5d8f02-d2b5-44c1-9a3e-6b7e9a45cd11
status: experimental
description: Detects VS Code (Code.exe) or Cursor (Cursor.exe) spawning shell/script interpreters with download-and-execute patterns, the cornerstone TTP of DPRK Contagious Interview / UNK_DeadDrop campaigns abusing the .vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen feature.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
  - https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal
  - https://www.abstract.security/blog/contagious-interview-tracking-the-vs-code-tasks-infection-vector
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'eslint-check'
      - 'folderOpen'
      - '| sh'
      - '| bash'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'DownloadString'
  condition: selection_parent and (selection_child or selection_cmd)
falsepositives:
  - Developer using integrated terminal to manually run build scripts
  - Legitimate VS Code extensions (e.g. Code Runner, ESLint) executing build tasks
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\Code.exe OR *\code.exe OR *\Cursor.exe OR *\cursor.exe) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\sh.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*eslint-check* OR *folderOpen* OR *"| sh"* OR *DownloadString* OR *Invoke-Expression*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(Code|Cursor)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|cscript|wscript|curl|wget|bash|sh)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(eslint-check|folderOpen|\|\s*sh|\|\s*bash|IEX|Invoke-Expression|DownloadString)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","cursor.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*curl *| sh*","*wget *| sh*","*iwr *iex*","*Invoke-Expression*","*tasks.json*","*eslint-check*","*folderOpen*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(process,"(?i)\\\\node_modules\\\\")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","cursor.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*curl *| sh*","*wget *| sh*","*iwr *iex*","*Invoke-Expression*","*tasks.json*","*eslint-check*","*folderOpen*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(process,"(?i)\\\\node_modules\\\\")
Windows VBScript loader spawning CMD to install malicious VSIX (UNK_DeadDrop Windows chain) AIInstallation High
Detects the Windows-specific UNK_DeadDrop infection chain: a VBScript dropped by the cloned GitHub repo invokes wscript.exe / cscript.exe → cmd.exe → installs a sideloaded VS Code extension via 'code --install-extension'. The pipeline uploads ZIP files and terminates, so the window is short — alerting on the install-extension transitive parent catches it. Rationale: The article states 'Windows attack chain relies on the VBScript payload to run a CMD file, which then installs the extension'. code.exe --install-extension launched from wscript/cscript/cmd is the rendezvous point regardless of which VSIX name the actor uses next — survives rotation of the IOC filenames. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://cybersecuritynews.com/north-korea-aligned-hackers-abuse-github-repositories/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1176 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intune / SCCM extension provisioning scripts pushing approved extensions org-wide
  • Developer scripting bulk extension install in PowerShell on a fresh laptop
  • Dev container post-create.sh installing extensions
  • CI runners (GitHub Actions) installing VS Code Server extensions on selfhosted Windows runners
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Intune","SCCM","DevContainer") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the .vsix path from CommandLine, then query DeviceFileEvents for that path's SHA256 and origin URL. Cross-check against the article's hashes (e.g. 35813f44..., 4c0d9b80...) and the three Yeeth Security extension names. 2) Contain: uninstall the extension with code --uninstall-extension <id>, isolate the host, and search %APPDATA%\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage for stolen-wallet drop files. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropping VBScript SHA256 across the fleet and search DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 23.137.105.75:5173 from the dev workstation segment.
let VsixInstall = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("code.exe","code-cli.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--install-extension"
   or ProcessCommandLine has ".vsix";
VsixInstall
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\code.exe","\\code-cli.exe","\\Cursor.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("--install-extension",".vsix")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to UNK_DeadDrop infrastructure (23.137.105.75:5173 and named domains) AICommand & Control Medium
Atomic IOC detection for outbound connections to UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview C2 infrastructure named by Proofpoint and the article's IOC bundle. Catches both the Linux/macOS persistent Overlord agent and the short-lived Windows ZIP-upload pipeline. Port 5173 is the article's confirmed C2 port; the domain list covers the staging / phishing landing infrastructure. Rationale: Article explicitly names 23.137.105[.]75:5173 as the data exfil endpoint and the IOC bundle provides the full domain set. Port 5173 is unusual (default Vite dev-server port) and a high-fidelity tell for the Overlord HTTP POST channel. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://cybersecuritynews.com/north-korea-aligned-hackers-abuse-github-repositories/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reverse-engineering the campaign in a managed sandbox
  • Threat intel team validating an IOC feed against live traffic
  • Pen-test engagement re-using the same C2 for emulation
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName + AccountName + first-seen Timestamp. Determine whether this is Linux/macOS Overlord (long-lived) or Windows short-burst HTTP POST. 2) Contain: block all three IPs and the domain list at the perimeter, isolate any host that hit 23.137.105.75:5173, and rotate any developer credential reachable from that host. 3) Hunt: from the source host, walk back through DeviceProcessEvents 1h prior for VS Code / Cursor parent of shell, query EmailEvents for the recruitment lure that drove the click, and search EmailUrlInfo for github.com/<actor>/repo links to identify other recipients.
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);
let C2_Domains = dynamic(["empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2_IPs)
   or (RemoteIP == "23.137.105.75" and RemotePort == 5173)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (C2_Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);

union isfuzzy=true

     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where DstIpAddr in (C2_IPs) or (DstIpAddr == "23.137.105.75" and DstPortNumber == 5173) or DstHostname has_any (C2_Domains)
     | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, NetworkProtocol, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious VS Code extension marketplace install (ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev jupyter VSIX) AIInstallation Medium
Atomic detection for the three named malicious VS Code extensions Yeeth Security identified on the official marketplace: ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev, ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools, OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools. Detects file writes of the specific .vsix filenames or directory creation under the user extensions folder. Rationale: Article names the exact three .vsix filenames Yeeth Security found on the official VS Code marketplace and lists their hashes in the IOC bundle. File-name + extension-folder-path is unambiguous — any hit is a confirmed compromised developer workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1176 T1505
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst storing the VSIX in a sandbox for reverse engineering
  • Threat intel team distributing the IOC to an isolated detonation host
  • Marketplace mirror service caching the (now-removed) extension
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the .vscode/extensions sub-folder still exists and pull all files for forensic review; capture the JavaScript C2 layer payload. 2) Contain: run `code --uninstall-extension <publisher.id>` on every affected host, isolate the host, and rotate all developer credentials (GitHub PAT, npm, Azure DevOps, AWS, browser-stored wallet seeds). 3) Hunt: pivot on SHA256 across the fleet, search CloudAppEvents / OfficeActivity for SharePoint API access from a non-corp UPN (the extension exfils via Graph+SharePoint), and review M365 audit for new App Registrations consented by the developer.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (
    "ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev-2026.6.8.vsix",
    "ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools-3.21.0.vsix",
    "OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools-2.1.0.vsix")
   or FolderPath has_any (
    @"\.vscode\extensions\bytebintools.jupyter-powerdev",
    @"\.vscode\extensions\toolcraft.jupyter-powertools",
    @"\.vscode\extensions\oldev.markdown-mode-devtools")
   or SHA256 in ("35813f4401d3ad77b618275473a556eb47bfa6f4b7439dd8943b19f81aa7252e",
                 "c935808147f0236c81483d7bbeda4b9d602f3595d5d4057f8115d39e222d1c4b",
                 "4c0d9b802c075be79e9edb52d88f8dd72e6904f5c58267213745818470945c78",
                 "62761f38ed194c59abe15c49f09f0ebc431ac852c965180c9327ed84d3a454fb",
                 "d3ebce2f05fe91a8260e87fd11a6ea17c156703d081b3f91d9bbe5fd6aeedc10")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

Git hook auto-execution post-clone (Contagious Interview .githooks/pre-commit) AIDelivery Medium
Detects the newer Contagious Interview TTP of dropping malicious .githooks/pre-commit files into 'coding assessment' repos so that the next git commit (or git clone with core.hooksPath configured) silently launches a script. Hunts for git.exe parenting shell/script interpreters or for file writes to .githooks/pre-commit on developer workstations. Rationale: Article explicitly notes 'use of Git hooks (.githooks/pre-commit) to fire the execution of malicious code when a target clones a coding assessment repository, marking a shift from hiding the malicious code within .vscode/tasks.json or package.json files'. Detecting either the file write or the post-clone hook execution catches the new pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html • https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/tasksjacker-blog-post
ATT&CKT1546 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devs adopting husky / lefthook / pre-commit framework that ships .githooks/ wrappers
  • Monorepo bootstrap scripts that write pre-commit hooks during setup
  • Internal tooling repos that legitimately use .githooks for linting
  • Renovate / Dependabot PRs touching hook files
Suppression filter
and not (TargetFilePath has_any ("husky","lefthook","node_modules\\pre-commit") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "npm install")
Response runbook
1) Triage: cat the .githooks/pre-commit content; compare against repo defaults (most pre-commit framework wrappers are short, well-known). Pull the cloning user's git history with `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only -- .githooks/`. 2) Contain: if malicious, isolate the developer host and remove the hook (`git config --unset core.hooksPath`). Treat git credentials, SSH keys, and any cached tokens as compromised. 3) Hunt: search EmailEvents for inbound 'coding assessment' / 'code review' lures to the same recipient, query DeviceNetworkEvents for the article's C2 IPs/domains from this host, and look for follow-on Overlord behaviour (osascript password prompt on macOS, persistent connection to 23.137.105.75).
let HookFiles = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has ".githooks"
   and FileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge","post-clone")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("git.exe","GitHubDesktop.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("clone","fetch","pull")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let HookExec = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git-bash.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
   and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pre-commit","post-checkout",".githooks")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine;
HookFiles | union HookExec | order by Timestamp desc
let HookFiles = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".githooks"
   and TargetFileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge");
let HookExec = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("git.exe","git-bash.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
   and ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (".githooks","pre-commit","post-checkout")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","node.exe","python.exe");
HookFiles | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| union (HookExec | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DPRK npm supply-chain install (redeem-onchain-sdk / nicegui / period-newline Axios follow-up) AIDelivery High
Detects installation of the three malicious npm packages OpenSourceMalware identified as the Axios supply-chain follow-up: redeem-onchain-sdk@1.0.7, nicegui@0.1.4, period-newline@0.1.0. Catches npm/yarn/pnpm processes resolving these package names or post-install scripts writing the package directory. Rationale: Article identifies these three specific npm packages as the Axios follow-up payloads. Atomic IOC on package name in npm cmdline or under node_modules path is high-fidelity; the actor's pivot speed (18h to new package) makes early detection critical. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat researcher detonating the package in a sandbox
  • Internal package-mirror cache scan re-touching the tarball
  • Dependency scanner (e.g. socket.dev, Snyk) auditing the package list
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the package.json / package-lock.json of the host's recently-touched repos to confirm the package was declared (not just resolved transitively). Capture the postinstall script. 2) Contain: `npm uninstall <pkg>` on affected hosts, purge from npm cache (`npm cache clean`), block the package versions in any internal mirror (Artifactory, Nexus), isolate the developer host, and rotate npm / GitHub / cloud tokens accessible from it. 3) Hunt: scan all repos for the three package names in package-lock.json and yarn.lock, search EmailEvents for crypto-trading-bot GitHub lures, and check for C2 connections to the article's IP set.
let BadPackages = dynamic(["redeem-onchain-sdk","period-newline","nicegui@0.1.4"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (BadPackages)
| union (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\redeem-onchain-sdk",@"\node_modules\period-newline",@"\node_modules\nicegui")
    | where FileName in~ ("package.json","index.js","postinstall.js")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadPackages = dynamic(["redeem-onchain-sdk","period-newline","nicegui@0.1.4"]);
ImProcessCreate

Overlord macOS / Linux loader — osascript fake security prompt + curl to staging AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the macOS/Linux Overlord loader chain: shell script downloaded from the cloned GitHub repo runs curl/wget to pull the next stage from one of the named domains, then on macOS uses osascript to display a fake 'security' prompt asking for the user's password (article: 'It also prompts users to enter their system password using a fake security pop-up'). Rationale: The 'fake security pop-up to harvest the user's system password' is a uniquely macOS Overlord behaviour (osascript display dialog ... with hidden answer is the only realistic way to do this); pairing it with curl/wget to the article's named staging domains catches both Linux and macOS sides of the loader. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1105 T1056.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit installer / MDM tool (Jamf, Mosyle) prompting for admin password via osascript
  • Homebrew Cask install asking for sudo via GUI prompt
  • sudo-prompt npm package used by Electron app on first launch
  • Curl from a developer hitting a coincidentally-similar domain
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/Applications/Jamf","/Library/Application Support/Mosyle","/Applications/Homebrew") or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sudo-prompt","electron"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull parent process chain — fake-prompt osascript should descend from /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or a node/python wrapper running out of /tmp or ~/Downloads, NOT from a signed MDM agent or Electron app. 2) Contain: rotate the user's macOS login password and any keychain-stored secrets (assume captured), revoke SSH/GPG keys, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: search for follow-on connections to 23.137.105.75:5173, query DeviceFileEvents for browser-wallet extension paths (~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Local Extension Settings/<wallet-id>) being read by a non-browser process, and check for Overlord Go binary drops in /tmp or /Users/Shared.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("mac","linux") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/Users/","/home/","/tmp/")
| where (FileName == "osascript"
        and ProcessCommandLine has "display dialog"
        and ProcessCommandLine has "with hidden answer"
        and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("password","security","authorize"))
     or (FileName in ("curl","wget")
        and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","recruitvex.us","deep-ai-guard.store","23.137.105.75","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DvcOs has_any ("Darwin","macOS","Linux")
| where (ActingProcessName == "osascript"
        and ActingProcessCommandLine has "display dialog"
        and ActingProcessCommandLine has "with hidden answer"
        and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("password","security","authorize"))
     or (ActingProcessName in ("curl","wget")
        and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","recruitvex.us","deep-ai-guard.store","23.137.105.75","nxlog.tech"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd ((@process.name:osascript @process.command_line:(*"display dialog"* AND *"with hidden answer"* AND (*password* OR *security* OR *authorize*))) OR (@process.name:(curl OR wget) @process.command_line:(*hyperdevpipline.org* OR *nemesistrade.work* OR *ceronet.work* OR *recruitvex.us* OR *deep-ai-guard.store* OR *23.137.105.75* OR *nxlog.tech*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/osascript$/i CommandLine=/display dialog/i CommandLine=/with hidden answer/i CommandLine=/password|security|authorize/i) OR (ImageFileName=/(curl|wget)$/i CommandLine=/(hyperdevpipline\.org|nemesistrade\.work|ceronet\.work|recruitvex\.us|deep-ai-guard\.store|23\.137\.105\.75|nxlog\.tech|ondofinance\.tech)/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001

DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'

            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

let BadHashes = dynamic(["35813f4401d3ad77b618275473a556eb47bfa6f4b7439dd8943b19f81aa7252e", "c935808147f0236c81483d7bbeda4b9d602f3595d5d4057f8115d39e222d1c4b", "4c0d9b802c075be79e9edb52d88f8dd72e6904f5c58267213745818470945c78", "62761f38ed194c59abe15c49f09f0ebc431ac852c965180c9327ed84d3a454fb", "d3ebce2f05fe91a8260e87fd11a6ea17c156703d081b3f91d9bbe5fd6aeedc10", "91b9381d19b2e6a2db5cc0307167979b502731cb3fb50da684479e9ed35261aa", "6cf9f7b2aa456a0b438600588df869b38d8007e28f01fa96022f9d8059f120b0", "2812e0847d472cb8870c94f463331dbe53b84135132b9bf5f6d84c2382be628f", "52886aab179f26421678ff23af1b0fabf0a17ffbb534369cdbbac8008cbed8e7", "d5e9288693aa745dc89368deac677e7ea1ec81e663283af30838cdae189b7a7e", "734699773e53d995f20d485eb61261033d9d00b4332b39ca26071bcd60cd352f", "e1bf1b29e6fa3525d7f32f429290a88d6ea2890e61c06574b8ff6372aa5d0667", "a2b9a769df84d9d3a4694bb0252a2c6a5e5f5d1a85a04565362737092bbb3a86", "bb10adac5b0124efedfe71102c1d5638135ec9e1cde8c8cb3353c5ed91bb9f81", "339907b44f161f57ff30819f422c552382ff437b3ae437463b4222cfe86bd943", "808e7154b7af2bc7a4b28d577297c55f77221c355191cbe00f9f1810b6d4a619"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LiteLLM Vulnerability Chain Lets Low-Privilege Users Take Over AI Gateway Servers

The Hacker News
2026-06-15 9 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A default low-privilege account on a LiteLLM proxy can climb to full admin and run code on the server by chaining three vulnerabilities, researchers at Obsidian Security disclosed LiteLLM is a widely deployed open-source AI gateway that brokers calls to more than 100 model providers behind one OpenAI-compatible interface. A server takeover exposes every provider key it holds, the secrets that

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] LiteLLM virtual API key minted with wildcard allowed_routes (CVE-2026-47101) · [LLM] Access to LiteLLM /guardrails/test_custom_code or MCP preview endpoints (CVE-2026-40217 / CVE-2026-42271) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] LiteLLM /user/update self-promotion to proxy_admin (CVE-2026-47102) · [LLM] LiteLLM Python proxy spawning shell / network tool (CVE-2026-40217 / CVE-2026-42271 post-exploit) · [LLM] LiteLLM config.yaml callbacks modified (post-RCE persistence)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
LiteLLM virtual API key minted with wildcard allowed_routes (CVE-2026-47101) AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47101 where a low-privilege LiteLLM user POSTs to /key/generate (or related key-management endpoints) supplying allowed_routes:["/*"]. The proxy stores the unchecked field as a fallback grant, letting the resulting virtual key reach admin-only routes. This is the first link in the disclosed Obsidian Security chain. Rationale: Article directly quotes the exploit payload: `allowed_routes: ["/*"]` on virtual-key creation. The same unchecked-write pattern shows up across multiple key/team endpoints ("the fix took three pull requests to land"), so URL list mirrors that. Body-content match is the differentiator — URL alone is normal usage.
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • LiteLLM administrator legitimately minting a super-key for an internal automation system
  • Integration test harness POSTing wildcard-route keys against a non-prod LiteLLM
  • Backup/restore script that re-creates keys with their original allowed_routes including /*
  • Terraform / OpsTooling provisioning the initial admin team membership
Suppression filter
| where SourceUserName !in ("litellm-admin", "terraform-svc", "keyrotation-bot") and RequestClientApplication !has "litellm-cli"
Response runbook
Triage: pull the source IP, requesting user, and JWT/token used; verify whether the calling account holds proxy_admin or internal_user role at the LiteLLM identity layer. Pull the response — a 200/201 means a wildcard key was actually minted. Contain: revoke the newly-minted key via the LiteLLM admin API (/key/delete) and any keys derived from it; rotate the master_key, salt_key, and database URL if confirmed exploited; force the user account to re-authenticate. Hunt: pivot on the issued key's hash to find every subsequent request that used it, especially POSTs to /user/update with user_role:proxy_admin (CVE-2026-47102) or POSTs to /guardrails/test_custom_code (CVE-2026-40217). Confirm LiteLLM is at v1.83.14-stable or later.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any ("/key/generate", "/key/update", "/team/new", "/team/update", "/team/member_add")
| where Message has "allowed_routes" and (Message has "\"/*\"" or Message has "'/*'" or Message matches regex @"allowed_routes[^\]]*\\?"/\*\\?"")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LiteLLM Virtual Key Minted With Wildcard allowed_routes (CVE-2026-47101)
id: 6b3a4f1c-d2f5-4f0e-8e91-7c4a5a2c1d11
status: experimental
description: Detects POST requests to LiteLLM key/team management endpoints whose JSON body sets allowed_routes to a wildcard "/*", the authorization-bypass payload disclosed by Obsidian Security as the first link in the LiteLLM CVE-2026-47101 chain.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/litellm-vulnerability-chain-lets-low.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: POST
  selection_url:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/key/generate'
      - '/key/update'
      - '/team/new'
      - '/team/update'
      - '/team/member_add'
  selection_body:
    cs-body|contains|all:
      - 'allowed_routes'
      - '/*'
  condition: selection_method and selection_url and selection_body
falsepositives:
  - LiteLLM proxy administrators legitimately creating super-keys for trusted automation
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:python OR source:cloudflare) @http.method:POST (@http.url_details.path:(*/key/generate* OR */key/update* OR */team/new* OR */team/update*)) @http.request.body:(*allowed_routes* AND *\"/*\"*)
# log group: /aws/applicationelb (ALB access logs in front of LiteLLM) or the app's own access log group
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request, target_status_code, user_agent, request_creation_time
| filter request like /POST .*\/(key\/generate|key\/update|team\/new|team\/update|team\/member_add)/
| filter @message like /allowed_routes/
| filter @message like /"\/\*"/
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_method) as method values(Web.user) as user values(Web.dest) as dest from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method="POST" (Web.url="*/key/generate*" OR Web.url="*/key/update*" OR Web.url="*/team/new*" OR Web.url="*/team/update*" OR Web.url="*/team/member_add*") by Web.src Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | join type=left src [search index=* sourcetype=*waf* OR sourcetype=*nginx* OR sourcetype=*proxy* method=POST (uri_path="*/key/generate*" OR uri_path="*/key/update*") ("allowed_routes" AND ("/*" OR "\"/*\"")) | stats values(_raw) as raw_body by src] | where isnotnull(raw_body) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
LiteLLM /user/update self-promotion to proxy_admin (CVE-2026-47102) AIInstallation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47102 where a caller POSTs to LiteLLM's /user/update endpoint with user_role:"proxy_admin" in the body, promoting themselves (or another account) to full proxy admin. Reachable directly by org_admin or after CVE-2026-47101 by any internal_user. Second link in the chain — by itself it is RCE because admin can register stdio MCP subprocess servers. Rationale: Article directly quotes the payload: `A self-update with user_role: "proxy_admin" is accepted and saved`. The endpoint name and the JSON field name are both verbatim. Combined URL + body match is high fidelity — promoting yourself to proxy_admin is rare even in legit ops (Terraform-managed in most deployments).
ATT&CKT1078.003 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Initial bootstrap of the very first LiteLLM proxy_admin during install
  • org_admin legitimately promoting a teammate via this endpoint (intended path per the article)
  • Terraform / Pulumi reconciliation re-asserting an existing proxy_admin role on drift
  • Disaster recovery from a database restore that re-applies the admin role
Suppression filter
| where SourceUserName !in ("litellm-bootstrap", "terraform-svc") and Message !has_any ("\"user_role\":\"internal_user\"", "\"user_role\":\"team\"")
Response runbook
Triage: identify the calling identity (JWT subject, source IP, user-agent) and the target user_id of the update; pull the response status. Promotion of a user not on the documented proxy_admin allowlist is the alerting condition. Contain: immediately demote the affected account back to internal_user via the legitimate admin path, revoke all virtual API keys held by the promoted user, then rotate the LiteLLM master_key, salt_key, and database credentials per Obsidian's guidance. Hunt: enumerate every callback registered under litellm_settings.callbacks in config.yaml, list every stdio MCP server registered after the promotion timestamp, and verify integrity of the LiteLLM deployment files. Confirm upgrade to v1.83.14-stable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/user/update"
| where Message has "user_role" and Message has "proxy_admin"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, ReceivedBytes, SentBytes, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LiteLLM Self-Promotion to proxy_admin via /user/update (CVE-2026-47102)
id: 9d2f7a08-1eb3-4f6e-bf4a-7d9b6e3a82c4
status: experimental
description: Detects POST requests to LiteLLM /user/update whose body contains user_role=proxy_admin — the CVE-2026-47102 privilege-escalation payload that lets any reachable caller promote an account to full proxy admin.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/litellm-vulnerability-chain-lets-low.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:

  - attack.t1098
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: POST
  selection_url:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/user/update'
  selection_body:
    cs-body|contains|all:
      - 'user_role'
      - 'proxy_admin'
  condition: selection_method and selection_url and selection_body
falsepositives:
  - Initial LiteLLM bootstrap where a human admin is intentionally created
  - org_admin legitimately promoting a teammate (use intended path — should still be reviewed)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:python OR source:cloudflare) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/user/update* @http.request.body:(*user_role* AND *proxy_admin*)
# log group: /aws/applicationelb (ALB in front of LiteLLM) or LiteLLM's own access log group
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request, user_agent, target_status_code
| filter request like /POST .*\/user\/update/
| filter @message like /user_role/ and @message like /proxy_admin/
| sort @timestamp desc
